Delta Technical Troubles
Hundreds of Delta flights
were delayed
yesterday after a technical issue prompted an FAA ground stop and, later, a ground delay for Delta-bound flights at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.
The issue, which was resolved by evening, lies with Delta’s weight-and-balance system, used to calculate an aircraft’s total weight. That system also determines a plane’s center of gravity and its weight distribution. It is unclear what caused the outage as of this writing; the company temporarily switched to a manual workaround to maintain passenger safety. Nearly 1,000 Delta flights depart from Hartsfield-Jackson on peak travel days. Yesterday's hourslong outage had ripple effects for other Delta flights across the country (see
hub-and-spoke model 101
Hartsfield-Jackson is the world's busiest airport by passengers, handling 106.3 million fliers in 2025. More than 4 million passengers are expected to pass through the airport this Thanksgiving season—a 5% jump from 2025. (Driving instead? Here are the best and
worst times to do it
; scroll for chart.)
Major Mathematics Milestone
A mathematician employed by Anthropic says he
solved a 167-year-old math problem
by collaborating with the company’s artificial intelligence tool, marking the second time AI helped unravel a
Millennium Prize Problem
this year. Independent researchers confirmed the validity of the proof over the weekend.
In 1859, German mathematician Bernhard Riemann proposed that there is a pattern to explain the distribution and spacing of prime numbers as the number line grows toward infinity. With the knowledge that prime numbers become increasingly rare as one continues counting up, Riemann created a formula to estimate how many primes exist below any number. Watch an explanation
here
Confirming the Riemann Hypothesis long eluded mathematicians because it required proving a pattern held across infinite prime numbers without any exceptions. Levent Alpöge was able to guide Anthropic’s large language model Claude to express a proof over 17 million lines of code.
The feat comes about two months after OpenAI announced its system had produced a proof for the
Navier-Stokes problem

Roundup Settlement
Bayer is on track to
pay up to $7.3B
to resolve around 65,000 claims alleging its Roundup weedkiller causes a type of blood cancer. The agreement, approved by a Missouri judge, follows a 2020 settlement that saw Bayer agree to pay approximately $10B across more than 100,000 claims.
Eligible claimants exposed to Roundup through farming, landscaping, or home lawn care receive tiered payouts averaging $10K to $165K, covering both existing and future non-Hodgkin lymphoma diagnoses. At issue is
glyphosate
, an herbicide Bayer began removing from residential Roundup in 2023. The Environmental Protection Agency maintains glyphosate is unlikely to cause cancer when used as directed, citing a 2018 study of over 54,000 pesticide sprayers that found no link to non-Hodgkin lymphoma. However, a 2019 analysis focusing on the most highly exposed groups found exposure to glyphosate may
increase the risk
of non-Hodgkin lymphoma by up to 41%.
Health experts say occasional residential use—like for lawn maintenance—often poses minimal danger, as risks are primarily linked to prolonged exposure.
